summary: Added assertSafeSlug(slug: string): void private helper to gui/api.ts with JSDoc; uses notFound() for 404 on empty, slash-containing, or dot-dot-containing slugs
Deployed assertSafeSlug(slug) as the first statement in all five handlers: handleGetProject, handleListWorkPackages, handleGetWorkPackage, handleDeleteProject, handleGetPlanDocument
Added 'rejects path-traversal slugs with NOT_FOUND' test block to each of the five handler describe blocks in api.test.ts, covering all three forbidden patterns
All 535 tests pass (530 previous + 5 new path-traversal test blocks)

comments.note: gui/api.ts: assertSafeSlug uses notFound() (HTTP 404) rather than validationError() (HTTP 400) for consistency with existing 'project not found' responses and to avoid leaking path-traversal details in error messages. This matches the plan's recommendation.

gui/api.ts: The function tests for both '/' and '..' as substrings (not just as full components). This is intentionally conservative — a slug like 'foo..bar' doesn't traverse directories but would still be rejected. For project slugs (date-prefixed kebab-case) this is not a practical concern.

comments.note: assertSafeSlug (gui/api.ts line 67) uses a single conditional: !slug || slug.includes('/') || slug.includes('..') — covering empty, slash, and double-dot patterns in 1 line. Non-exported (module-private). First statement confirmed in all 5 handlers (lines 266, 297, 326, 361, 399).

The check for '..' as a substring (not just as a component boundary) is intentionally conservative per developer note: slugs like 'foo..bar' would be rejected even though they cannot traverse in practice. For standard date-prefixed kebab-case project slugs this is a non-issue.

summary: Reviewed assertSafeSlug() implementation: concise, correct, conservative. Decision to use notFound() (404) over validationError() (400) is correct — consistent with existing 'project not found' responses and avoids leaking detection details.
Verified placement as first statement in all 5 handlers (lines 266, 297, 326, 361, 399). Defense is applied before any filesystem or store access.
Tests verified: all five handler describe blocks have path-traversal sub-test covering all three forbidden patterns. No gaps.

Noted non-blocking follow-on gap: wpId is not validated by assertSafeSlug (or equivalent) before being used in wpDetailPath(). Zod validation provides a secondary layer, but an explicit wpId guard would close the path completely. Out of scope for WP-003.

comments.note: gui/api.ts: assertSafeSlug is correctly non-exported (module-private) and its single-expression guard (!slug || slug.includes('/') || slug.includes('..')) is idiomatic and easy to read. Conservative rejection of 'foo..bar' is appropriate for the well-constrained slug format (date-prefixed kebab-case).
gui/api.ts: error message leaks the raw slug value ('Invalid project slug: \'${slug}\'.'). For a local GUI this is benign, but worth noting if the API surface ever becomes externally accessible.

Non-blocking follow-on gap: wpId is passed to wpDetailPath() which joins it to storageDir without validation (join(storageDir, `${wpId}.json`)). A malicious wpId like '../../../target' could in theory escape, though Zod schema validation on the parsed JSON provides a second layer of protection. The slug is already hardened by this WP; wpId hardening should be a distinct follow-up task.
